title: Yeast library creation using the SWAT method
protocol: Clone the desired genomic modification into a donor plasmid.
Transform the donor plasmid into a SWAT donor strain containing SGA procedure genetic traits.
Cross the donor strain with the SWAT library.
Perform mating between the strains.
Select diploids from the mated cells.
Induce sporulation in the selected diploids.
Select haploids after sporulation.
Select double mutants for further analysis.
Replicate double mutant plates onto galactose-containing media to induce swapping of desired modules into the genome.
Select positively swapped yeast by 5-FOA negative selection for the SWAT acceptor module.
Perform additional selection using a marker introduced with the donor module.
Transform the donor plasmid into a SWAT donor template strain using the standard Saccharomyces cerevisiae PEG/LiAC transformation protocol.
Test the swapping capability of the cloned donor plasmid on a few strains.
Verify that test strains have the same traits as the SWAT donor template strain, including an additional SWAT acceptor module in the genome.
Tag specific proteins with the SWAT module (plasmid pST-N2) to create testing strains if not provided with the library.
Transform the donor plasmid into the test donor strains according to the selection specified in the donor plasmid.
Incubate at 30°C for 2-3 days as per the transformation protocol.
Pick a few single colonies from each transformation and patch them onto fresh selection plates.
Incubate at 30°C for 1-2 days.
Either pick and re-patch or replica plate the yeast onto plates containing 2% galactose media (YPGal).
Incubate at 30°C for 1-2 days.
Repeat the induction step on YPGal plates another time.
Pick and re-patch or replica plate the yeast onto plates with selection media specified in the protocol.
Incubate at 30°C for 1-2 days.
Repeat the selection step another time.
Perform an experiment to test the swapping of the donor module, comparing yeast from before (step 2) and after (step 5) swapping.
Cross the SWAT donor strain with the SWAT library to create haploid, double-mutant yeast.
Use the Singer RotorHD colony arrayer for high-throughput library plate manipulation.
Transfer yeast from one selection media to another using the Singer RotorHD colony arrayer or a manual pinner (V&P scientific).
Test growth of strains on an extra plate with the same media at each step as a control for the selection used.
Plate the original donor strain and several colonies from the library array on diploid selection media (#4) before mating.
Plate the original donor strain and strains from the library after SceI induction (#13).
Transfer plated strains to Swap selection (#14) to verify that they do not grow.
Check that blank locations did not get contaminated during plate replication at various stages.
Perform PCR analysis using swapped and original colonies.
Plan primers to test for the presence of the new tag in the yeast genome.
Ensure primers confirm no non-swapped yeast remain after swap of N’ SWAT-GFP libraries.
Conduct functional analysis on positive and negative control gene colonies based on introduced module.
Assess percent of swapped vs. non-swapped clones after streaking swapped colonies to single colonies.
